The pump must overcome all three simultaneously. Discharge pressure ≠ TDH."}, {"mistake": "Ignoring friction loss in short pipe runs (<50 m).", "correction": "Even short piping with elbows and valves contributes measurable friction loss. Always add 20–30% to the straight-pipe equivleant length for fittings."}, {"mistake": "Assuming municipal water pressure remains constant during peak demand.", "correction": "Pressure drops significantly when municipal supply is shared. Conduct a 24-hour pressure survey and design to the minimum sustained pressure documented."}, {"mistake": "Selecting pump based solely on nameplate capacity without verifying the actual operating point on the pump curve.", "correction": "Pump curves show how flow, head, and efficiency vary. Operating at the design point (center of curve) ensures maximum reliability."}, {"mistake": "Forgetting to account for sclea buildup in older pipes when applying Hazen-Williams C values.", "correction": "Use C = 100–110 for pipes >10 years old instead of C = 120 for new pipe to predict actual friction loss accurately."}]} />
